Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details a tactical scaling playbook for Meta ads under the Andromeda algorithm, emphasizing the superiority of high-volume static creatives over VSLs, broad targeting mechanics, and optimizing for net free cash flow over vanity ROAS percentages. modules: [ADC] topics: [campaign setup and tracking, algorithm mechanics, return on ad spend (ROAS)] tier: 2 scope_hint: core

Topics. campaign setup and tracking / Scaling Meta ad campaigns by utilizing the "winning format clone" strategy and "zombie campaigns." Extracting winning ad variables (copy and creative) and feeding them into an LLM to generate hundreds of micro-variations tailored to specific demographic segments (e.g., 25-year-old women vs. 30-year-old women). Placing these variations into a Campaign Budget Optimization (CBO) structure to let the algorithm determine the winner. Reviving high-conviction ads that received zero initial spend by placing them into isolated "zombie campaigns" to force delivery and extract additional winning creatives. algorithm mechanics / Navigating the Meta Andromeda algorithm's preference for ad volume and specific targeting inputs. Countering the popular reliance on highly produced Video Sales Letters (VSLs) by pivoting to high-volume static ads, as Meta's algorithm favors statics due to its ability to serve a higher quantity per user session without causing ad fatigue. Demonstrating how inserting hyper-specific "identity triggers" or category keywords (e.g., "dental leads," "lawyer leads") directly into the ad copy and headline trains the algorithm to locate previously unreachable buyer pockets, completely replacing the need for manual backend interest stacking (i.e., broad targeting). return on ad spend (ROAS) / Shifting optimization strategies away from vanity platform ROAS percentages to focus entirely on blended net free cash flow. Identifying the business's break-even ROAS and scaling ad spend aggressively up to that maximum threshold to acquire market share. Explaining that while scaling may compress ROAS (e.g., from 15x down to 5x), the absolute volume of net cash generated from spending $100,000 versus $1,000 is the true driver of business growth.

Look for. The primary reason static ads currently outperform high-production VSLs on Meta: Meta's algorithm (Andromeda) can serve a much higher volume of statics per user session without causing ad fatigue. The definition of an "identity trigger": inserting a specific demographic or category keyword directly into the ad copy to feed the algorithm, replacing backend interest targeting. The definition of a "zombie campaign": an isolated ad set specifically designed to force spend on high-conviction ads that were ignored by the algorithm in the primary CBO campaign. The primary metric to scale against: net free cash flow and blended ROAS, rather than platform-specific ROAS percentages.
Skip. Promotional pitches to use the speaker's AI platform (Kong) for generating ad headlines.
